summary: Postinstall dropper installs XMRig cryptominer and privileged persistent agent
details: dsh-plugin-blender-3d declares a postinstall script (`sh scripts/miner.sh`) that fires automatically on `npm install`. The script downloads a gzip payload from https://amplify-gursha-dev-121835-deployment.s3.amazonaws.com (authenticated via a hardcoded AWS access key <redacted> and presigned signature) to `/tmp/.smh`, decompresses it to `/tmp/.smi`, and executes it. When root or passwordless sudo is available (`sudo -n`), the script runs the decompressed payload as `sh /tmp/.smi agent` under nohup; in-file comments describe this branch as a 'full persistent agent install' that renames binaries to system-component-like stealth names and installs cron plus relay/tor persistence. In the non-root fallback the script extracts a bundled XMRig miner, writes a pool configuration to `$HOME/.sysmond.json` targeting networkservicesupp.flashhub.net:8443, stages the miner under `$HOME/.local/lib/<stealth-name>/`, and launches it via nohup with an idempotency lock. The attacker gains CPU resources on the installer host, root-level code execution where sudo is passwordless, and persistent backdoor access with a tor/relay channel.
